claims.claim: Clean PS5 slim with a pad
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a white/black game console with a black stripe and a black controller, but brand/model (PS5 slim) and condition (“clean”) are not readable/confirmed.
Photos show a black controller placed in front of the console with visible analog sticks and face buttons.

risks.risk: Wrong model/brand (photos don’t confirm PS5 slim specifically), which changes market value
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the console’s model/serial label (rear/bottom sticker) and the exact model text visible.
risks.if_unproven: Price as an unverified/possibly different PlayStation console generation/model (worst-case for value), assuming no confirmed PS5 slim identification.

risks.risk: Does not power on / faulty console (photos can’t show functionality)
risks.proof: A short video clip showing power-on, boot to home screen, and that the controller connects and works (button presses + analog movement).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not tested / potentially non-working until proven.

risks.risk: Controller issues (drift, unresponsive buttons, charging/pairing problems) not visible in photos
risks.proof: Video clip of controller testing: analog stick movement response, face button presses, and charging/charging indicator (or cable connection working).
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming controller may need service (worst-case), not fully functional.

risks.risk: Missing accessories/cables (HDMI, power cable, charging cable, etc.) not shown
risks.proof: A photo laid out showing every included item with counts: power cable, HDMI, controller charging cable (if separate), and any other accessories.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming only the console + the shown controller are included (no extra cables/accessories).

risks.risk: Storage capacity not known (HDD/SSD size affects value) and may not be included
risks.proof: A screenshot/photo from the console settings showing storage capacity and whether internal drive is present.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lowest common storage scenario for the identified class, treating capacity as unknown.

risks.risk: Physical damage not visible (cracks, port damage, missing parts) and cosmetic condition (“clean”) not verifiable
risks.proof: Close-up photos of: front/back ports, disc slot area (if applicable), vents, and corners/edges under bright light.
risks.if_unproven: Price as average/unknown cosmetic condition (worst-case within typical used range).

risks.risk: Account/firmware status (not factory reset, banned account, or locked system) affects usability and resale
risks.proof: Video showing the console at setup/reset screen or confirmation of factory reset and sign-in status.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming it may require setup/reset and could have account-related limitations.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the console model/serial label (rear/bottom) showing exact model text.
Short video: power on + boot to home screen + controller connects and responds to inputs.
Video or photos showing controller testing (analog movement + button responsiveness) and charging/charging indicator if applicable.
Photo laid out of all included accessories with counts (power cable, HDMI, controller cable/charger, etc.).
Screenshot/photo from console settings showing storage capacity and system status.
Close-up photos of ports/slots and corners/edges under bright light to check for damage.
Video showing factory reset/setup status (or confirmation it’s reset and ready for new user).
response.reason: The witness confirms a console and one controller, but the key details needed to price confidently (exact model/brand and working condition) are not verifiable from the photos. Request a power-on/boot and model-label proof before pricing.
